import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 942

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/942](https://www.erdosproblems.com/942)
-/

open Nat Filter Topology

namespace Erdos942

/--
Let $h(n)$ count the number of powerful integers in $[n^2, (n + 1)^2)$.
-/
def erdos_942.h (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ((Finset.Ico (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2)).filter Powerful).card

/--
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,
$h(n) > (\log n)^{c - o(1)}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_942 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c > 0, ∃ (o : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    (∀ᶠ n in atTop, erdos_942.h n < (Real.log n) ^ (c + o n)) ∧
    {n | erdos_942.h n > (Real.log n) ^ (c - o n)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
It is not hard to prove that $\limsup h(n) = \infty$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_942.variants.limsup :
    atTop.limsup (((fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (n : ℕ∞)) ∘ erdos_942.h)) = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/--
It is not hard to prove that the density $\delta_l$ of integers for which $h(n) = l$ exists
and satisfies $$\sum_l \delta_l = 1$$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_942.variants.density :
    ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, ∀ l, {n | erdos_942.h n = l}.HasDensity (δ l) ∧
    ∑' l, δ l = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos942

reformulations.difference: The 1976 primary source counts powerful numbers in (n²,(n+1)²), whereas Lean counts them in [n²,(n+1)²).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Including the powerful number n² adds exactly one. This identity was checked in Lean. All three claims are invariant: adding one preserves limsup = infinity; the positive logarithmic-exponent bounds absorb an additive constant through an exponent adjustment of order 1/log(log n); and the densities are reindexed by δ₀ = 0 and δₗ₊₁ = dₗ, preserving their existence and total sum 1. Including n = 0 is likewise immaterial to these asymptotic statements. The complete invariance argument, beyond the counting identity, was not formalized in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The primary paper uses arbitrary-ε upper and infinitely-often lower bounds with an exponent α. Lean uses a positive exponent c and one common error sequence tending to zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The ε-bounds and null-sequence formulation are equivalent by choosing increasing cutoffs for ε = 1/k and increasing lower-bound witnesses; conversely, convergence of the error gives each ε-bound. Sharing the error does not strengthen the assertion: independent errors u,v tending to zero can be replaced by |u|+|v|, since log n > 1 eventually. This shared-versus-independent-error equivalence was proved in Lean. Positivity is also harmless relative to the paper's unsigned α: simultaneous Dirichlet approximation using k distinct squarefree b = O(k) produces k distinct powerful numbers a²b³ within the two square intervals adjoining an integer q, with log q = O(k log k). Thus some interval has at least k/2 such numbers, at indices tending to infinity; any exponent satisfying the paper's upper bounds must therefore be at least 1. The full equivalence with the paper's formulation was not proved in Lean.

sources_consulted: P. Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions, Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (1976), pp. 25–44, especially p. 35 (PDF page 11): https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerful_number — definition, equivalence with square-times-cube representation, and initial values.
https://teorth.github.io/erdosproblems/ and https://teorth.github.io/erdosproblems/app.js — database interface and identification of its underlying data source.

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Nat/Full.lean; FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Data/Set/Density.lean; Mathlib's asymptotics, limsup, extended-natural, real logarithm, and real-power definitions.
review.notes: All four declarations were checked against the primary paper. The cited landing page https://www.erdosproblems.com/942 repeatedly returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so any newer webpage-only remarks or status changes could not be checked directly. The independent database currently records the problem as open, consistent with the file; the primary paper explicitly describes both auxiliary claims as not hard to prove. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings and contains 24 checked examples, including small h values, the prime-divisor meaning of Powerful, little-o equivalence with convergence to zero, ordinary natural-density semantics, summability forced by tsum = 1, and the equivalence of the ENat limsup statement with ∀ N M, ∃ n ≥ N, M < h(n). No repository files were modified.
